explanation: The siege that ended the possession the conquest began, and the one place the articles state the span outright. “Siege of Malacca (1640–1641)”, at revision 1370743206 — the revision that record already cites — opens: “The siege of Malacca (3 August 1640 – 14 January 1641) was initiated by the Dutch East India Company and their local ally, Johor, **against Portuguese Malacca**”, and its § Background says when Malacca became that: “Malacca, established by the Malays in the 1400s, was a significant hub of trade toward the beginning of the 16th century. **It was conquered by the Portuguese Empire in 1511**”. “Malay–Portuguese conflicts” at revision 1370627478 closes the arithmetic from the other side: the siege ended “nearly 130 years of official Portuguese presence in the region”. `precondition-of` and not `caused`: the 1640–1641 article puts the roots of the conflict in the Dutch arrival of the late sixteenth century and the Company’s years of attempts, not in the conquest; what the conquest supplies is the Portuguese Malacca the siege was against. `probable`, on the two articles alone (rule 22).
